rule: Butcher first; at the case, grass-fed and pasture-raised.
checks: Ask the butcher what the animal ate and how it lived.
Liver and heart count too; add one now and then.
Packaged meat: meat, salt and spices, nothing else.
beyond: Find a butcher who knows the farm, and ask what came in today.

rule: Hens on pasture, cows on grass, dairy with few ingredients.
checks: Read how the hens lived before anything else.
Pick cheese with a short label and nothing added.
beyond: Find a farm with eggs and milk; ask what the hens eat.

rule: Organic on anything you eat the skin of.
checks: Buy it whole and in season.
Turn berry boxes over; the bottom tells the truth.
beyond: Try the farmers market this week; much of it was picked days ago.

rule: Wild-caught first, and ask where it was caught.
checks: Ask the counter where and how the fish was caught.
beyond: Find a fishmonger who can name the boat, and keep going back.

rule: Choose packages with a short list of real ingredients and only natural fats: tallow, olive oil, coconut oil.
checks: Skip seed oils and avocado oil, whatever the front of the package says.
The ingredient line tells more than the front; read it first.

rule: Frozen counts as whole when the bag lists the food and nothing else.
checks: Frozen meals follow the pantry rule: real ingredients, natural fats.
Pick bags frozen solid, not clumped.
